title: Pluggable policy fabric and audit-first middleware for RBAC v2
creator: Marina Delgado
description: Scope: build a pluggable policy fabric for RBAC v2 that unifies policy evaluation across the public API, internal runtime gateway, and the admin console. Deliver an "audit-first" authorization middleware that always emits structured, tamper-evident audit events and supports audit-only mode for gradual rollouts. Goals: (1) consistent decision semantics for API/runtime/console, (2) sub-2ms median evaluation latency for cached decisions, (3) streaming audit events to the audit pipeline with signed envelopes, (4) seamless SSO/SAML group claim enrichment and admin controls.
details:
Design highlights and trade-offs:
- Policy substrate: use a lightweight compiled policy format (policy bytecode) instead of evaluating Rego at runtime to reduce overhead. Policies are authorable in a high-level DSL and compiled to the bytecode during CI. Trade-off: adds a compilation step and a small learning curve for policy authors, but reduces tail latency and enables deterministic caching.
- Evaluation model: attribute-based entitlements tree with fast path short-circuiting for allow/deny decisions and negative caching for explicit denies. Support partial evaluation for requests missing attributes (defer decision).
- Middleware placement: provide SDK middleware for API gateway, a runtime interceptor for model-serving nodes, and a web-auth middleware for the console. All three share the same evaluation library (C ABI) compiled for our runtime.
- Caching: two-level cache: request-scoped KV cache for token->principal resolution and a global LRU decision cache keyed by (principal-hash, resource, action, context-hash). Eviction policy tuned for high-cardinality keys (session granularity).
- Audit-first: every evaluation emits a structured audit event with fields: request_id, correlation_id, principal_hash, policy_version, decision, matched_rules, reason, ttl_hint. Events are signed with KMS HMAC and pushed to our audit topic with backpressure handling.
- SSO/SAML: enrich principal with group claims at sign-in time; runtime middleware accepts enriched JWTs and validates signature. For SAML-asserted attributes that exceed size limits, fetch group membership via a secure graph lookup and cache results.
- Admin controls: support admin-scoped exemptions, emergency bypass (audit-only toggles), and a per-tenant policy override table. Overrides are recorded as higher-priority policy fragments and are auditable.
- Observability: extensive metrics (decision latency histogram, cache hit ratio, policy compile failures), trace spans, and per-policy evaluation counters.
- Security: all policy fragments stored encrypted at rest, policy compilation runs in a hermetic CI container, and audit events are signed to provide tamper evidence.
- Rollout strategy: feature-flagged rollout with audit-only stage -> sampled enforcement -> full enforcement. Start with non-customer-facing internal routes then expand to Dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Unified evaluation library published and vendored into runtime and console. 2) Middleware implemented for API gateway and runtime interceptor. 3) Audit events emitted for 100% of evaluated requests and ingested by audit pipeline. 4) End-to-end test coverage for allow/deny/partial decisions including SAML group enrichment. 5) Performance: median eval latency <2ms cached, p99 <40ms uncached on staging hardware. 6) Security review completed and KMS-based signing enabled.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: high cardinality principals (API keys, service accounts) may poison caches. Mitigation: normalize principal identifiers and limit TTLs; apply negative caching heuristics.
- Risk: SAML group fetches add latency. Mitigation: asynchronous enrichment with best-effort immediate fallback to nominal deny/partial decision plus automated retry.
- Risk: policy bugs could cause incorrect denials. Mitigation: audit-only rollout window, formal policy unit tests, and a fast rollback path via policy-version pinning.
